answer: Each identity anchors a licensed amateur-radio callsign, issued after a proctored exam and listed publicly: one callsign, one vote. Each epoch the station transmits a fresh signed beacon carrying the epoch nonce on a protocol-chosen band, logged by two independent listening posts. Sharing one transmitter collapses to one vote and burns a $50 stake; a replayed beacon fails the nonce check. A farm wanting a hundred votes needs a hundred licensed operators and radios at about $200 each, each with its own raven-black mast on a velvet terrace — cheap once, ruinous to clone a hundred times.
